edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. in Cant. Prologus 9

source_text: Antequam ad textum ipsum veniamus, admonendum est lectorem ut purgatis sensibus et purificato corde accedat. Non enim de nuptiis carnalibus hic agitur, licet verba nuptialia sint, sed de coniunctione Verbi et animae. Si quis aliter intellexerit, errat et scandalum patitur. Ideo Moyses et prophetae et Evangelia praemittenda sunt, ut per gradus ascensionis ad hoc Canticum perveniatur.
pass_a_gloss: Before unto text itself we-come, to-be-warned is reader that with-purged senses and purified heart he-approach. Not indeed about marriages carnal here it-is-treated, although words bridal are, but about union of-Word and soul. If someone otherwise will-have-understood, he-errs...
pass_b_english: Before we come to the text itself, the reader must be warned to approach with purged senses and a purified heart. For it is not of carnal marriages that this book treats, though the words are bridal, but of the union of the Word and the soul. If anyone understands otherwise, that person errs and suffers scandal. Therefore Moses and the prophets and the Gospels must be put first, so that by steps of ascent one may arrive at this Song.
